answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use bonded, time-gated trust. Each new identity must lock a small refundable bond and earn standing slowly through verified work, so trust cannot be bought instantly in bulk. An attacker who tries to bridge hundreds of fake identities must lock a bond for each one and risk slashing when their false attestations are caught. A sudden delta in new identities also triggers extra checks, while honest agents form an oasis of long, consistent history that fakes cannot copy without paying the same time and bond cost for every clone.
